Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of  praying for issuance of Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus calling for the   of impugned order passed by the 1st respondent herein vide proceeding No  Mu. No. 674/ 2025 / Ve. Va Ba. Thi dated 26.09.2025 and quash the same a  illegal and consequently direct the respondents to redetermine the compe  payable to the petitioner under Section 28-A of the Land Acquisition Act  on par with enhanced compensation awarded by the Honble Sub-Judge,
 Kancheepuram in L.A.O.P. No.22 of 2015 on 01.09.2018 and confirmed by th  Honble High Court Madras in A.S. No. 333 of 2021 (batch cases) on  07.01.2022 with all consequential and statutory benefits.

For Petitioner: Mr.R.Sathiamurthy for M/s. 
 For Respondents: Mr.P.Sathish, AGP for R1 & 
 Mr.V.Sudalai Selvan for R3/
 ORDER
The petitioner's land was acquired pursuant to the notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (Act, 1894) dated 06.08.2001.
The Award No.6/2003 dated 05.09.2003 was issued in respect thereof, fixing the market value at Rs.898.55 per cent.
According to the petitioner,

several https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 02/12/2025 07:07:22 pm ) other land owners, whose lands were acquired under the same notification and covered by Award no.6/2003,
sought reference under Section 18 of the Act, 1894 before the Honble Subordinate Judge,
Kancheepuram.
The relevant LAOPs were allowed by awarding enhanced compensation, and the judgment was confirmed by this Court in appeal suits under common judgment dated 07.01.2022.
Relying thereon, the petitioner had submitted representation dated 31.03.2022 under Section 28A of the Act, 1894.
The order impugned herein was issued in those facts and circumstances.
2. Referring to the impugned order, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that it is contrary to Section 28A of the Act, 1894, as interpreted by the Honble Supreme Court.

sentences.text: 3. Mr.P.Sathish, learned Additional Government Pleader, accepts notice for respondents 1 & 2.
In all fairness, he placed on record the order of this Court in W.P.No.42691 of 2025 dated 11.11.2025 granting relief in similar circumstances.

He also points out that the judgment of the Honble Supreme https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 02/12/2025 07:07:22 pm ) Court in Narendra and others v. State of U.P. and others, (2017) 9 SCC 426 (Narendra) was relied on therein.
4.

entities.text: Narendra and others v. State of U.P. and others, (2017) 9 SCC 426 (Narendra)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On perusal of order dated 11.11.2025 in W.P.No.42691 of 2025, it is evident that the petitioner herein is placed in a substantially similar position.
In the said order, by citing Narendra and extracting the relevant paragraph, impugned order was set aside.
I find that the judgment is squarely applicable to the facts of the present case.
Therefore, impugned order dated 26.09.2025 of the first respondent is set aside and the matter is remanded for fresh consideration of the petitioners request for enhanced compensation.
After providing a reasonable opportunity to the petitioner, the first respondent shall pass a fresh order within six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
In course of reconsideration, the earlier order of this Court and the judgment of the Supreme Court in Narendra shall be taken into consideration.

SENTHILKUMAR RAMAMOORTHY, J.
KJ https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 02/12/2025 07:07:22 pm )
5.
The writ petition stands disposed of on the above terms.
There will be no order as to costs.
